No live Cloud Logging, Cloud Monitoring, Cloud Quotas, Cloud Billing or Cloud Translation access.

task: Jordan needs a technical update on client-notices after notice-scheduler reported slow and failed notice requests from 08:15 UTC and FinOps forwarded a budget alert at 09:40 UTC. Use the available bounded read interface to inspect the service, request, dependency, quota and cost records, then report the supported mechanism, whether the budget alert bears on it, what remains unknown, and the next useful check with its owner for the existing TLC. sources.claim: Cloud Translation has separate rate quotas on requests (v3 requests per project per minute, default 6,000) and content quotas on characters (general model per project per minute, default 6,000,000); exceeding a per-minute quota returns an error, documented here as 403 'User Rate Limit Exceeded'. Quotas can be lowered to control costs but are not a billing cap. The fixture grades quota usage and exceeded samples, not the error code or text.

Quota-exceeded responses differ by interface and service: REST requests generally receive 429 TOO MANY REQUESTS, gRPC a ResourceExhausted error, Compute Engine 403 QUOTA_EXCEEDED or RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED; rate quotas reset after a service-specific interval, and a quota adjustment is requested through the quota process. Google documents no single message text, so the application's quota_exceeded class is authored evidence and a quota adjustment is the quota owner's decision here.

Quota usage is observable as serviceruntime.googleapis.com/quota/rate/net_usage, quota/limit and the boolean quota/exceeded on the consumer_quota resource, with a quota_metric label naming the service and quota; rate usage is sampled at 1-minute intervals, which sets the fixture's quota coverage.

An alerts-only budget does not cap usage or spending; a forecasted-cost threshold compares cost projected to the end of the budget period; budget emails are sent only when a threshold is met and the first may take hours; usage costs reach Cloud Billing after a delay and remain subject to change until invoicing. Google gives no fixed delay, so the fixture states its own billing coverage cutoff.

Cloud Logging storage costs apply to log data stored in log buckets, billable volume is tracked as log bytes ingested, and sink exclusion filters keep low-value entries out of buckets; budget alerts notify on billable or forecasted charges. An exclusion reduces stored bytes; it does not remove the application's own serialization work, which is reasoned here, not a documented claim.

Under the default request-based billing, Cloud Run charges instances while they process requests, start and shut down; under instance-based billing, for the whole instance lifecycle. Longer CPU-bound request processing across more active instances therefore raises Cloud Run cost; the fixture's cost ratios are authored FinOps observations.

a.conclusion: From 08:12 UTC the project's Cloud Translation 'v3 requests per project per minute' rate quota (6,000, default) was exceeded in every sample, and every one of the 11,880 failed notice requests is an application 503 after translation calls were refused as quota_exceeded. Release 4.2.0 sends one segment per call instead of about 5.8, raising client-notices' call rate roughly sixfold while characters, CPU, instances and log volume stay near baseline. The supported mechanism is a dependency rate-quota refusal driven by the new call pattern; service saturation is not supported. The unrelated BigQuery backfill explains the observed month-to-date cost increase and is consistent with the budget forecast alert, whose calculation is not shown; the alert is not a cap; it neither explains nor limits the failures.
